proposal.description: The cycle-boundary strobe fires on the falling edge of pwm_sync (high-side turn-off, the peak) instead of the rising edge (end of low-side conduction, the valley).
proposal.reason: Each window sample is taken at PWM falling edges, so the cp_delay value BLANK_CLKS clocks before high-side turn-off is counted. When cp_sync is high only during the low-side period (or only during the high-side period), fault_count_*_out and window_trip/window_trip_SS differ from the valley-sampled reference.

proposal.description: The blanking history cp_delay advances once per switching cycle (on pwm_rise) instead of once per clock, so the lookback is BLANK_CLKS cycles rather than BLANK_CLKS clocks.
proposal.reason: While active, the sample added at each pwm_rise is the comparator state from several switching cycles earlier, not from a few clocks before turn-on. A burst of overcurrent shows up in fault_count_*_out and the trip outputs several cycles late, and a cp_sync pulse just before one turn-on is missed.

proposal.description: The S_RUN window samples the live cp_sync at pwm_rise instead of the blanked cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1] value from before high-side turn-on.
proposal.reason: In S_RUN, a cp_sync that is high at the turn-on edge but was low BLANK_CLKS clocks earlier (or the other way round) is counted differently. fault_count_run_out and window_trip change, while the S_SS path is unaffected.

proposal.description: The soft-start count adds the live cp_sync while the SS shift register stores the blanked cp_delay sample, so the count and the window contents diverge.
proposal.reason: In S_SS, when cp_sync at pwm_rise differs from cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1], the count gains or loses one against the window. fault_count_ss_out drifts, and can wrap when the bit leaves 32 cycles later, so window_trip_SS asserts or fails to assert wrongly.

proposal.description: The soft-start count adds the previous cycle's sample (fault_shifter_SS[0]) as the entering bit instead of the new sample being shifted in.
proposal.reason: In S_SS the count lags the window by one switching cycle and covers only 31 cycles. After a sustained overcurrent, window_trip_SS asserts one cycle late, and it never asserts when trip_ss equals WINDOW_SS.

proposal.description: The S_RUN window is rewritten to insert the new sample at the MSB and shift right, but the count still subtracts bit WINDOW_RUN-1 as the leaving bit, which is now the newest sample.
proposal.reason: In S_RUN the count subtracts the sample added one cycle earlier instead of the one 16 cycles old. fault_count_run_out never rises above 1 during sustained overcurrent (and wraps when faults stop), so window_trip does not assert for trip_run of 2 or more.

proposal.description: The soft-start window and count are cleared on every S_RUN sample, instead of being held through S_RUN for telemetry.
proposal.reason: After the S_SS -> S_RUN transition, fault_count_ss_out drops to 0 at the first pwm_rise in S_RUN. It should keep the value reached at the end of soft start.

proposal.description: The S_RUN window is also advanced during S_SS, so it enters S_RUN pre-loaded with soft-start overcurrent history.
proposal.reason: fault_count_run_out becomes nonzero during S_SS when cp_delay is sampled high. On entry to S_RUN, window_trip can assert immediately because of faulted cycles that happened during the expected soft-start inrush.

proposal.description: The idle clear of both windows is qualified by pwm_rise like the update branches, so the windows clear only if PWM is still toggling while neither state is active.
proposal.reason: When the converter leaves S_RUN/S_SS and pwm_sync stops (or no rising edge comes before re-entry), the counts are not cleared. fault_count_*_out keep their old values in idle, and the retry starts on the old history, so the trip asserts again early.

proposal.description: The idle clear resets the two counts but leaves the two shift registers holding the faulted history from before the hiccup.
proposal.reason: After a retry, the old 1s shift out of the window and are subtracted from a count that was cleared to 0. fault_count_*_out wrap to a large value and window_trip / window_trip_SS assert without any new overcurrent.

proposal.description: The S_RUN threshold is truncated to the 5-bit run-count width instead of the count being widened to TRIP_W, so trip_run values of 32 and above lose their top bit.
proposal.reason: With trip_run set to 32 or more (meant to be unreachable, since WINDOW_RUN is 16), the truncated threshold is small or 0. window_trip then asserts in S_RUN with few or no faulted cycles.

why: make lint already catches it: make lint: UNUSEDSIGNAL

proposal.description: window_trip is gated by 'not in soft start' instead of 'in S_RUN', so it is not suppressed in the idle states.
proposal.reason: On the clock S_RUN is left with fault_count_run at or above trip_run, the run count is cleared only at the next edge. window_trip therefore stays high for one clock outside S_RUN.

proposal.description: window_trip_SS is gated by 'converter switching' (S_SS or S_RUN) instead of S_SS only, so the frozen soft-start count can trip it during S_RUN.
proposal.reason: If fault_count_ss reached trip_ss on the edge the FSM left S_SS, or trip_ss is lowered during S_RUN below the held count, window_trip_SS is high throughout S_RUN.
